blocks.text: Information disclosure is the unintended exposure of source code, credentials, internal paths, configuration, version data, personal data or debugging output. By itself it is often low severity, but exposed secrets, source maps, VCS metadata and backups frequently lead directly to account or infrastructure compromise. This category collects the paths, headers and errors worth probing. For default paths and credentials also see `Security-Misconfiguration/`.

items: Backup, temporary and editor files; archived source (`.zip`, `.tar.gz`, `.bak`, `~`, `.swp`)
JavaScript source maps and bundled secrets
Debug endpoints, framework actuators, profilers and status pages
API documentation, GraphQL introspection and schema files
Verbose errors and stack traces; directory listing; user enumeration through messages and timing
Response headers and HTML comments revealing versions and internal hosts
Cloud storage and CI artifacts left public

blocks.text: Probe from a small, polite wordlist and read the status, size and content type of every hit. A real finding contains sensitive data, not just a 200 for a path that returns the home page (soft-404). Verify by checking that the content is what the path suggests: a `.git/HEAD` containing `ref:`, a `.env` with `KEY=value` lines. Report credentials as exposed without using them. Rate-limit your requests and stay within scope.
See `information-disclosure-payloads.txt`. Paths are relative to the application root and common sub-paths.
